Design: organize_at_rest(revisions, admissions, open_findings, body_marker_key) -> bool returns `not organize_gap(...)` verbatim — the criterion says the pre-query IS the gap's cardinality, so it is derived from that one function rather than restating any clause of it; an incoherent snapshot raises there for the same reason the gap raises. organize_gap's own signature and body are untouched (tests/chains/test_organize.py pins its parameter set).

Admissions fed to the pre-query are the ones the owner already holds in memory, deduped to the latest judgment per surface across phases (new OrganizeOwner._judged_surfaces). That dedupe is needed because each phase records verdicts under its own key and organize_gap refuses duplicate admissions per surface; without it the first phase's stale view (taken before the criteria phase created the criterion child) would falsely say "not at rest". Crucially the pre-query does NOT re-run OrganizeAdmission.is_live: is_live reads a revision AND re-reads the whole scope through OrganizeContextReader, so any liveness re-check would itself cost N scope reads and make "one obligation read per tick" unachievable. Body liveness is still checked — organize_gap compares each admission's admitted_body_digest against the body digest in the same snapshot, which is pure arithmetic over the single read. The one thing the pre-query therefore cannot see is a graph-context change (a relation edit) that touches no body: such a scope reads as at rest for that tick. That is the direct consequence of "answer from the same single read"; the per-round gap computation inside the loop keeps the stricter is_live filter unchanged.

Read cost for a scope that has work is unchanged: the opening snapshot is carried into the first convergence round (`unspent`) instead of being read again, so no second tracker read was introduced anywhere.
